column3: It supplies the closest ordered-gathering parallel: a mixed force is mustered and held in ranks.
It adds that gathering can expose presumed allies as enemies.
It identifies the Fire as a commanded punitive realm, though not the procession into it.
It closely repeats the judgment-day gathering and restraint of a denying cohort.
It immediately continues the arrival at the Fire with bodily testimony against the gathered enemies.
It adds the Fire's overpowering force against both humans and jinn.
It contributes the basic public-gathering action without the judgment or Fire setting.
The repeated prophetic message and painful punishment do not clarify the controlled gathering.
It supplies a limited contrast between God's supporters and their enemies.
It portrays leaders directing others toward the Fire and losing all help at judgment.
The arrival of a clear messenger does not add to the gathering-to-Fire scene.
The origin of jinn from fire does not clarify their being gathered to it.
It names the Fire as the enduring recompense for God's enemies in the same surah sequence.
It develops the tribunal after arrival: the skins explain their testimony by divine speech.
The racing oath image does not add to the hostile crowd's ordered procession.
It joins a total human-jinn gathering to questioning and a lasting abode in the Fire.
The earth's provisions do not clarify the judgment procession.
It states that death and killing end in gathering to God, without the hostile or Fire setting.
It adds repeated exposure to the Fire followed by entry into the severest punishment.
It identifies the concealed conduct and false assumption behind the bodily testimony.
It only states that disbelievers face punishment of the Fire.
It defines enemies through hostile conduct, but not their eschatological gathering.
It supplies the same surah's prior refusal to hear or receive the call.
It connects disbelief in purposeful creation with woe from the Fire.
It provides the inverse path: former enemies are united and rescued from the Fire.
It shows worldly intimacy reversing into enmity on the Day, except for the mindful.
It confirms the inability to rescue one already in the Fire.
It offers a bodily image of confinement and forced posture, without the gathering scene.
It states that their false judgment of their Lord brought about their ruin.
It identifies persistent disbelievers as companions of the Fire.
It depicts people rushing after inherited tracks, a limited precursor to compelled movement.
It links human and jinn loss to companions who beautified their course in the same surah.
It gives a general dispersal-and-return-to-God gathering pattern.
It warns that leaning toward wrongdoers brings contact with the Fire.
It adds the same surah's denial of the Hour and promised disclosure of deeds.
It describes the Fire prepared for disbelievers, but not the gathered tribunal.
It affirms an inevitable universal gathering for the Day of Resurrection.
It advances the parallel mustered cohort into direct questioning over denial of signs.
It links excess to becoming companions of the Fire and return to God.
It connects aggression and wrongdoing with return to severe punishment on the Day.
It completes the parallel judgment sequence with a binding sentence and silence.
It turns prior denial into direct recognition of the Fire before them.
It contrasts being restrained in ranks with a prayer to be directed toward grateful action.
It uses the same directing verb for a prayer that ordered resolve serve gratitude and repair.
It shows Pharaoh initiating a coercive citywide muster, an inverse political gathering.
It presents the Fire as the place where the deniers are tested directly.
The report of knowledge beyond a royal force only weakly extends the parallel muster scene.
Its crisis prayer and rival attachment do not add to the procession or tribunal.
It gives a leader who goes before his people on the Day and leads them into the Fire.
The test of a messenger's report does not clarify the judgment procession.
It depicts the condemned dragged on their faces in the Fire and commanded to taste it.
It explicitly gathers criminals on the Day, though without their destination or restraint.
The trumpet blast marks the Day but does not add to the gathered enemies.
It gives gathering without the human judgment or Fire context.
It directly portrays criminals driven to Hell as a delegation.
It identifies the Day as difficult without adding its procession or outcome.
It states the enduring Fire abode of disbelievers in general terms.
It joins being gathered on faces to Hell with their worst place and most errant path.
The drowning of an angering people does not add to the focus's final gathering.
It only gives a general return and gathering to God.
It commands that the false worshippers be guided onto the path of Hell.
It affirms that the wise and knowing Lord gathers all people.
It supplies the trumpet-driven arrival in successive groups.
It frames the Fire as the rival destination against which salvation is offered.
It depicts people forcefully pushed toward the Fire of Hell.
It identifies disbelievers as the worst creatures abiding in Hell, despite the contrary route evidence.
The descent of angels on the Day does not clarify the hostile gathering.
It links wrongful killing with becoming a companion of the Fire.
It adds total gathering, brief worldly duration, and the loss of those who denied meeting God.
It directly combines total gathering with interrogation of those who associated partners.
It extends the gathered-idolater tribunal by questioning the objects they worshipped.
It only says wealth and children cannot avert the enduring Fire abode.
The description of persistent disbelievers does not add to the procession or tribunal.
It gives a general exhortation grounded in eventual gathering to God.
It shows disbelievers presented to the Fire, made to acknowledge truth, then commanded to taste punishment.
The question about kindling fire does not clarify the punitive destination.
It depicts faces turned in the Fire with regret over refusing God and the messenger.
It supplies only a warning of a blazing Fire.
It adds Pharaoh's assembled public call but is redundant after the coercive muster parallel.
It associates choosing error and punishment with endurance before the Fire.
It names God's kindled Fire without adding the gathering or judgment action.
The hot Fire description does not clarify who is gathered or how.
The fueled Fire description does not clarify the procession or tribunal.
It adds Fire, divine non-speech, and painful punishment for concealing revelation.
It joins gathering on faces, disabled senses, and an ever-renewed Hell abode.
The generic dispersal and return pattern is redundant after earlier gathering parallels.
It gives a destination in the Fire for those who set up rivals to mislead.
It combines total gathering with questioning angels about alleged worship.
It links worldly idol-based affection to mutual rejection, curses, and the Fire.
It connects transgression and wrongdoing to being made to enter the Fire.
The ongoing divine affair does not clarify the hostile gathering or Fire destination.
It defines false objects of worship as enemies, clarifying the opposing relation to God.
The messenger's refusal of payment and divine witness do not add to the focus scene.
It adds the inescapable Fire abode and repeated return of those who try to leave it.
The call to fear God and obey does not clarify the gathering-to-Fire scene.
It confirms that resurrection through the split earth culminates in an easy gathering for God.
It adds a portrait of people rushing into disbelief and facing great punishment.
The creation comparison used in Iblis's pride does not clarify the final Fire procession.
The account of magic and disbelief does not add to the gathered enemies or their destination.
It establishes enmity as a temporary earthly condition, without the final gathering.
It directly warns disbelievers that they will be gathered to Hell, closely matching the destination and collective judgment.
It explicitly says the disbelievers will be gathered to Hell after their futile opposition.
It gathers all people, separates the associators with their alleged partners, and orders them to remain in place for judgment.
It states that all are gathered with none left behind, supplying the totality of the final assembly.
It presents the gathered people before their Lord in ranks, clarifying the ordered tribunal implied by restraint.
It combines an oath to gather people and devils with their being brought kneeling around Hell.
It depicts everyone following the Caller without deviation, a close image of compelled, directed movement.
It places the worshippers and their false objects together as fuel entering Hell.
It commands the gathering of wrongdoers, their counterparts, and what they worshipped before their route to Hell.
It halts the assembled wrongdoers for questioning, extending the tribunal that follows their gathering.
It depicts disbelievers driven to Hell in groups, directly paralleling the hostile procession.
It adds shackles and chains around the condemned as they are dragged, sharpening the focus's image of restraint.
It completes the chained procession through scalding water and then into the Fire.
It shows every community kneeling and summoned to its record, adding a collective court posture.
It gathers the first and last generations for a fixed appointed day.
It names the Day of Gathering and its universal disclosure of gain and loss.
It commands that the condemned person be seized and bound before punishment.
It immediately directs the bound condemned person into the blazing Fire.
It gathers the present and former peoples on the Day of Decision.
It portrays Hell itself brought forward on the Day, completing the public judgment setting.
It calls every people with their leader, adding a cohort-based form of final summons.
It pairs the trumpet blast with the complete gathering of all people.
It depicts the trumpet-driven emergence from graves and hurrying toward the Lord.
It supplies the trumpet, universal collapse, revival, and standing in expectation before judgment.
It names the Day of Gathering and divides its outcome between Paradise and the Blaze.
